text.p: Severe weather with wind damage, flooding rains, hail, and tornadoes raked much of eastern Texas, Arkansas, parts of northern Mississippi and also portions of Tennessee, Kentucky, West Virginia, and southern Ohio on the weekend. The hardest-hit area in terms of tornadoes was Arkansas, with Kentucky getting the brunt of the flooding. Calmer weather moves into the region on Tuesday, with lingering showers coming to an end in Kentucky. Tranquil weather aids in cleanup efforts for the next few days.

Tropical cyclone Gavin will become an increasing risk to shipping in the southwest Pacific during this period. Winds are currently estimated at 50 mph but they should reach 65 mph in 48 hours and 75 mph in 72 hours. The system is currently east of the Santa Cruz islands, well north-northwest of Fiji. The system is moving east-southeast and thus will move away from the Santa Cruz islands while staying well north of Fiji during this period.
There are no further emergency statements at this time.
